items.title: 2026 Stephan Muller x Lost Origin; Dobe Mara - Panama
items.desc: This is a distinctive coffee and one of the few Maragogypes we have ever released. We are grateful to Stephan and Lost Origin for the work that went into producing it. In the cup we find dark berries, tamarind, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2026 Irma Quintero; El Refugio, New Season - Colombia
items.desc: This is our first year working with Irma Quintero and her very small Chiroso garden. While we have purchased few Chirosos from Huila, it is encouraging to see this variety being produced there. In the cup we find pomegranate, lemon zest, and lychee.

items.title: 2026 Banko Gotiti; Second Selection - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is our second selection of the season from the Banko Gotiti washing station in Gedeb. The site had an exceptional year, and we are glad to be able to share this second lot with you. In the cup we find nectarine, soft florals, and clementine.

items.title: 2026 Keramo - Ethiopia
items.desc: This lot comes from the extreme elevation of Karamo Village in the Bura zone of Sidama. The site is new to us, but we know and love the region. In the cup we find ripe berries, peach, and honeysuckle.

items.title: 2026 Flor Marina Betancourt; Finca Cataluña, First Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: This is our second release from Flor Marina, but the first of this new harvest cycle. Palestina produces some of our favorite Pink Bourbon profiles in Huila and we're excited for the opportunity to work with her coffee again this season. In the cup, we find raspberry, tangerine, and rosehips.

items.title: 2026 Juan Pablo Luque; Whua Whua Yoc, Competition Lot - Peru
items.desc: This was our highest-scoring lot in a local competition held near Inkawasi. In the cup we find orange blossom and complex tropical fruit, with exceptional structure.

items.title: 2026 Juan Carlos Gomez; Finca La Esperanza, First Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: Juan Carlos is a new producer in our Huila project, and this is our first time working with his coffee. In the cup we find Key lime pie, blueberry, and hibiscus.

items.title: 2026 Luis & Mildred Montoya; Finca Arboleda, First Harvest - Colombia
items.desc: We purchased our first lot from Luis this spring, and we are excited to welcome him back to the menu. Producing one exceptional lot in a year is challenging, and doing it twice is impressive. As our project in Urrao continues to thrive, we look forward to seeing what 2027 brings. In the cup we find a tropical profile of passion fruit, lemon zest, and cranberry.

items.title: 2026 Tamiru Tadesse Tesema; Safo, Washed - Ethiopia
items.desc: This is an exceptional separation from Alo's Safo site. The cherry comes from extreme altitudes and is a staggering example of the quality this special place can produce. In the cup we find a floral expression of honeysuckle, bergamot, nectarine, and silver needle.

items.title: 2026 Harold Ortiz Ceron; Finca La Cava, Chiroso - Colombia
items.desc: This is our second lot from Harold Ortiz Ceron, a new producer in San Pablo, Nariño. This Chiroso separation is the first Chiroso we have ever released from San Pablo. In the cup we find ripe strawberry, tangerine, and oolong.

items.title: 2026 Harold Ortiz Ceron; Finca La Cava, Pink Bourbon - Colombia
items.desc: This is a special release, as it is rare to see Pink Bourbon being cultivated in Nariño. We are honored to have been introduced to Harold Ceron, who is now producing many exceptional varieties on his new farm. In the cup we find blueberry, blood orange, and raspberry.

items.title: 2026 Chelbessa; 2nd Selection - Ethiopia
items.desc: Chelbessa has long been one of our favorite sites to work with in Gedeb, and we are pleased to welcome this year’s selection to the menu. In the cup we find stone fruit, citrus, and lemon verbena.

items.title: 2026 Sike Bokasso, White Honey - Ethiopia
items.desc: Sike Bokasso produces some of our favorite coffees in Guji, and this white honey preparation is no exception. In the cup we find melon, candied peach, and star fruit.

items.title: 2026 Elpidio Tabares; La Soledad - Colombia
items.desc: One of the longest and best seasons we have ever seen in Urrao has also brought new growth to our project there. In this lot, our first from Elpidio Tabares, we find passion fruit, lychee, and citrus.

items.title: 2026 Eulises Fabian Quilindo; El Higueron - Colombia
items.desc: This continues our slow shift toward the southern Huila season, and the exploration of the new Santa María region. In the cup we find bright red berries, lime, and wildflower honey.

items.title: 2026 Kanzu; Lot #16 - Rwanda
items.desc: This is our first release of the upcoming Rwandan season. We look forward to these coffees every year, and this lot is a fitting start. In the cup we find mulling spices, orange peel, and baked fruit.

items.title: 2026 Demeka Becha, Dry-Fermented - Ethiopia
items.desc: The Demeka site has produced some truly exceptional coffees over the years. This year, we selected exceptional dry-fermented and wet-fermented lots. In the cup we find lychee, black tea, and raspberry.

items.title: 2026 Pepe Jijon; Finca Soledad, TyOxy - Ecuador
items.desc: Pepe brings an artist’s intuition to his coffee, and this TyOxy lot is another stunning expression of his work. Compared with previous lots, it reveals a softer, more delicate side of a profile we have come to know well. In the cup we find hibiscus, the sparkling acidity of raspberry and tree tomato, and a subtle hint of fig.

items.title: David Berrio; La Casita, Curtain Call - Colombia
items.desc: This is the latest in the year we have ever received a harvest delivery from Urrao, and it comes from David Berrio. The quality has matched the occasion, and we are grateful this season has continued to deliver. In the cup we find nectarine, passion fruit, and honeysuckle.

items.title: 2026 Victor Dota, 2nd Harvest - Ecuador
items.desc: This Discord-exclusive lot from Victor Dota is exceptionally small, coming from his tiny 0.5-hectare (1.2-acre) farm. This coffee was taken straight off of the drying beds and flown to New York immediately. In the cup we find lemon zest, floral botanicals, and ripe stone fruit.

items.title: 2026 Pepe & Family; Finca Soledad Sidra Wave Natural, New Season - Ecuador
items.desc: This naturally processed Sidra comes from our dear friends Pepe and Jose Jijón, sourced exclusively for espresso for our collaboration with Motors. In the cup we find fruit punch, pineapple, and mango.

items.title: Huila Decaffeinated
items.desc: This decaffeinated lot is a blend of harvests from a small group of producers in San Agustín, Huila. In the cup we find a sweet and balanced profile of orange marmalade, dark chocolate, and strawberry.

items.title: Espresso - Footprints
items.desc: Let us introduce our espresso blend - Footprints. The name is borrowed from one of our absolute favourite jazz compositions with the same name, first released on Wayne Shorters album Adam's Apple in 1966. We love the name since it reflects our love for music as well as our firm belief that every part of the production chain has an impact on the final cup. Every part is important, everyone leaves a mark, everybody leaves a footprint. This has been a work in progress for many years and the time has now come to say farewell to Red Clay and Silent Shout. Although we have enjoyed working with two b

items.title: Timbuyacu
items.desc: Bourbon de Colasay, variedad de café arábica local única que se cultiva en el distrito de Colasay. Aunque los productores locales se refieren a ella como Bourbon debido a su apariencia similar, las pruebas genéticas sugieren que es una mutación o un cruce local que se asemeja genéticamente al Catimor, pero sin los sabores vegetales o astringentes comúnmente asociados a esa familia. En este lote en concreto dentro de la finca Timbuyacu, encontramos notas a nueces y avellana principalmente, junto con notas afrutadas que nos recuerdan a la pera y a la ciruela. Además, es un café con tacto muy dul

items.title: Kent
items.desc: Este Kent de Acacia Hills es nuestro café de la casa de Tanzania. Las notas principales son kumquat, almendra garrapiñada y pasas, a las que se suman miel cruda, piel de cítricos y cacao en polvo. Su cuerpo es redondo, como el de un dátil, y su acidez es media, comparable a la de un chocolate del 70 %.

items.title: OMBLIGÓN - LAS FLORES
items.desc: Este es uno de los lotes más singulares y experimentales que hemos tenido en NOMAD. Sus notas más distintivas nos recuerdan a cola de cereza, ruibarbo y caramelo de sandía, acompañadas de toques de ciruela negra, mosto de uva y caramelo de grosella. Tiene una acidez brillante y elevada, y un cuerpo sedoso que envuelve el paladar. Un café intenso y complejo, fruto de la variedad Ombligón y de un proceso de fermentación cuidadosamente controlado.

items.title: Esperanza
items.desc: En fragancia es muy dulce, con unas notas a pera y caqui. Además, podemos encontrar notas de panela, pasas y avellanas. El aroma sigue siendo dulce y aparecen notas de chocolate al 70% y de banana. En boca es denso, con un cuerpo almibarado y una acidez media y suave, como la de alguna fruta blanca. Un café equilibrado que funciona muy bien solo y aún mejor con leche.

items.title: Pacas
items.desc: Nos encanta este lote de Pacas de Carlos Pola por su perfil de cereza, canela y chocolate negro. A medida que se desarrolla en la taza, también aparecen nueces de California, manzana roja y azúcar morena. Su cuerpo es redondo y su acidez, media, nos recuerda a bayas y a chocolate.

items.title: Pacamara
items.desc: Nos encanta este Pacamara por su perfil dulce y afrutado. Destacan la mermelada de mandarina, la avellana y el azúcar moscovada, acompañadas de notas de chocolate con leche, ciruela amarilla y panela. Tiene un cuerpo cremoso, con una acidez suave que nos recuerda a la naranja confitada.

items.title: Primavera - La Papa
items.desc: Nuestro café de la casa de Huehuetenango, o “ciudad de los árboles” en lengua maya, ha llegado para quedarse con La Papa. Panela, mantequilla y pasas son sus notas principales, acompañadas de naranja, cacao nibs y avellana. Tiene un cuerpo cremoso y una acidez baja, muy bien integrada, que nos recuerda a la fruta pasificada.

items.title: Mi Finquita Lote M - Natural
items.desc: Este Geisha Natural de Mi Finquita se despliega con una intensa expresión frutal: frambuesas y frutos del bosque en un primer instante, acompañados por la dulzura tropical del mango maduro. En aroma, delicados matices de frambuesas liofilizadas se entrelazan con notas de té rooibos y té blanco. Su textura es sedosa y envolvente, mientras que una acidez fresca evoca la frambuesa y el dulzor de las fresas maduras y el mango aporta equilibrio y profundidad. Es expresivo y persistente, con un final de frutos del bosque que refleja el carácter vibrante y la complejidad de un Geisha Natural.

items.title: Mi Finquita Lote T - Lavado - Fermentado en vidrio
items.desc: Este Geisha Lavado de Mi Finquita se despliega con una brillante expresión floral: delicadas notas de flores blancas y osmanthus en un primer instante, acompañadas por matices de papaya madura y sutiles recuerdos herbales. Su textura es sedosa y limpia, mientras que una acidez fresca que evoca la granadilla se equilibra con el dulzor de la fresa madura. Es preciso y elegante, con un postgusto prolongado donde las notas florales reaparecen, dejando un delicado recuerdo a flor de saúco.

items.title: Mi Finquita Lote B - Lavado
items.desc: Este Geisha se despliega con una brillante intensidad cítrica: yuzu y pomelo rosado en un primer instante, acompañados por delicadas notas de miel de flores, nectarina y albaricoque. En boca, la acidez evoca la mandarina madura, mientras que el dulzor de melocotón y dátiles aporta profundidad y equilibrio. Su cuerpo sedoso recuerda la carnosidad de la guanábana, dando paso a un postgusto prolongado donde los cítricos reaparecen.

items.title: Mariana
items.desc: Un café natural goloso, dulce y con mucha profundidad. En la taza encontramos mora confitada, chocolate 70% y almendra garrapiñada como notas principales, acompañadas de mosto de uva, melaza y grosella negra. Su cuerpo es cremoso y deja un final a cacao en polvo. La acidez es media, con un carácter que recuerda a la fruta pasificada y que redondea una taza muy dulce.

items.title: Kii AB
items.desc: Nos encantan los cafés de Kenia por esa fruta intensa y esa acidez brillante. Este café de la estación de lavado Kii es un buen ejemplo de lo que nos gusta en los cafés kenianos. Podrás encontrar en taza notas a higo deshidratado, bergamota y una nota herbal que nos recuerda al té negro. Es un café con un cuerpo meloso, envolvente, muy dulce, con una acidez suave que nos recuerda a la acidez de la fruta deshidratada. También te puede recordar su aroma y sabor a ciruela, miel cruda y papaya. El retrogusto es largo y muy agradable.

items.title: Las Brisas
items.desc: Este café destaca por sus notas de chocolate con leche, nuez de California, y azúcar moreno, que ofrecen una experiencia cálida y reconfortante. A medida que se enfría, emergen sabores de galleta María, dátiles y un toque de almendra y pasas, añadiendo una profundidad interesante.

items.title: Julio Chávez
items.desc: Nos encanta este Geisha por su lado floral y delicado. En nariz destaca el jazmín, acompañado de una nota herbal que recuerda al té blanco y un toque de nectarina. En boca se vuelve más dulce, con matices de panela, miel y naranja que aportan redondez sin restarle finura. El cuerpo es ligero y elegante, con una acidez brillante y jugosa que cierra la taza con mucha frescura.

items.title: Albino Ibias
items.desc: En taza destacan la piña, el melocotón y la pera en almíbar, con matices de níspero, albaricoque y caramelo que se despliegan a medida que la taza se enfría. El cuerpo es almibarado y denso, con una acidez redonda y jugosa que envuelve el paladar. Un lote de trazabilidad de productor único, seleccionado para nuestra gama de Competición.

items.title: Alipio Palomino
items.desc: Nos encanta este lote de Alipio Palomino por su perfil floral, dulce y afrutado, tan propio de la Geisha Inca del valle de Incahuasi. En fragancia destaca la flor de naranjo, acompañada de notas a pasa sultana y chocolate blanco. En boca aparecen matices de fruta madura, chocolate con leche y orejones, sobre un cuerpo almibarado y una acidez melosa que redondean la taza.

items.title: Acacia Hills Pacamara
items.desc: Un café goloso y reconfortante, con notas a chocolate con leche, dátil y piel de cítricos que se despliegan desde la fragancia. En boca aparecen matices de mantequilla, pera y melaza, sumando dulzura y complejidad. Cuerpo meloso y acidez media, equilibrada.

items.title: Centroamericano Natural Anaeróbico
items.desc: Tranquilamente un café top 10 de nuestro menú año tras año. Un tipo de perfil que nos encanta en Nomad. Complejo y salvaje, con notas cremosas y afrutadas. Frutos del bosque, cerezas y cacao nibs en fragancia, dando paso a uvas y tamarindo al entrar en contacto con el agua. Cuerpo aterciopelado, acidez vinosa, y un retrogusto muy elegante de cacao en polvo.

items.title: Karimikui
items.desc: Uno de los cafés con más cuerpo e intensidad que hemos tenido en el menú de NOMAD. Su fragancia nos recuerda a la fruta de hueso, a la miel y a la panela. En cuerpo es intenso, con una acidez brillante y un cuerpo aterciopelado. Este lote de café con proceso lavado de Kenia nos ha trasladado años atrás en el tiempo, a la mejor época de este país en términos de calidad.

items.title: Bombe Natural
items.desc: En los cafés de proceso natural de Etiopía es muy característico encontrar notas a arándanos, chocolate con leche y dátil. Y este lote tiene todo eso y un poquito más. Hemos encontrado notas a fruta confitada, granada y lúpulo acompañadas de un cuerpo cremoso y una acidez jugosa haciendo de este lote, que tenemos cada año, un café muy agradable y complejo.

items.title: Shakiso Hadeso
items.desc: Un café con una fragancia muy dulce y con notas florales que nos recuerdan al lemongrass y a la flor del almendro. También encontramos notas herbales como té blanco. En boca es muy dulce, con una acidez suave y un cuerpo meloso. Cacao en polvo, melón verde y physalis son otras notas que hemos encontrado en este clásico café de Etiopía de proceso lavado.

items.title: Geisha Timbuyaku
items.desc: Un café muy floral, típico de la variedad Geisha. Podemos encontrar notas a té blanco y flor de saúco junto a notas afrutadas que nos puede recordar a la nectarine y a la ciruela. Un Geisha lavado riquísimo y disfrutón que nos encanta en NOMAD. Tiene una acidez suave y un cuerpo aterciopelado con un retrogusto largo y muy agradable.

items.title: Churupallana
items.desc: En fragancia y aroma es un café muy dulce con notas que nos recuerdan a frutos secos y cacao. En boca siguen presentes estas notas, pudiendo ser más específicas, podríamos encontrar notas a nueces y dátiles. Además, hay ligeras notas afrutadas que nos recuerdan a pera y a ciruela amarilla. Tiene un cuerpo denso, una acidez suave y un retrogusto muy agradable.

items.title: Nemba
items.desc: En fragancia es muy dulce, con notas a fruta deshidratada como los orejones. Estas notas son muy características de los cafés de lavado de Burundi que tanto nos gustan. También podemos encontrar miel y notas florales a flores blancas. Tiene una acidez melosa y un cuerpo sedoso. El retrogusto es largo y agradable y te deja una sensación en boca melosa y dulce como a miel.

items.title: Gahahe
items.desc: Este café destaca por su perfil vibrante con notas florales, mandarina y piña asada. En boca, ofrece un equilibrio perfecto entre dulzura y acidez jugosa, complementado por matices sutiles que lo hacen ideal para filtro. Su carácter afrutado y fresco lo convierte en una opción excepcional para disfrutar en cualquier ocasión.

items.title: Diego Mestas
items.desc: Dátiles, ciruela amarilla y níspero definen este café dulce y complejo de Cusco. Caramelo, almendras y chocolate con leche emergen en la taza, sostenidos por un cuerpo redondo y una acidez jugosa. Una experiencia de filtro refinada y equilibrada.

items.title: Descafeinado - Chambakú
items.desc: Más rico de lo que muchos piensan, este Chambakú Descafeinado presenta notas muy balanceadas y dulces de chocolate 80% y azúcar moscovado. Es un café con una acidez muy suave, un cuerpo muy redondo, y muy fácil de beber con leche, además de tener un ligero retrogusto a manzana golden que también hará las delicias de los cafeteros más exigentes.

items.title: Guatemala Finca Soledad Gesha - Cafe Only
SNSC Colombia Gerson Mora Ortega Pink Bourbon Natural
Ecuador El Dorado Wush Wush
items.desc: El Dorado is a high-elevation farm in Loja, Ecuador, established in 2017 by the Elder family in partnership with Bernard Uhe, combining Colombian generational expertise with Ecuadorian terroir. Cultivating Geisha, Wush Wush, SL28, and Sidra, the farm has earned multiple Cup of Excellence and Golden Cup placements, reflecting its precision-driven approach to producing exceptional coffees.

items.title: Panama Hacienda Esmeralda Leon Gesha
items.desc: Few producers have shaped specialty coffee quite like Hacienda La Esmeralda. Since the Peterson family's groundbreaking discovery of Gesha's potential in 2004, their pursuit of quality has continued to redefine what's possible in coffee. We've worked directly with the family since 2019, building a relationship through annual selections, visits to their farms in Boquete, and a shared curiosity for exceptional coffee. Today, we're proud to continue representing their work, celebrating the innovation and dedication behind each new harvest.

items.title: Krampus
items.desc: As sounds of concern fill the air in our roastery each holiday season, we know Krampus has made his annual appearance. This year, he set his sights on a special Kenya Peaberry from Kamunyaka Washing Station, part of the Iria-Ini Farmers Cooperative Society. Built in collaboration with station management through careful peaberry separations throughout the harvest, this lot showcases the distinctive character of Kenyan coffee.

items.title: Framily
items.desc: We’re delighted to share the return of our annual Holiday Coffee, a joyful, crowd-pleasing release that captures the spirit of gathering. This year’s offering comes from Bensa, Ethiopia, sourced through our partners at Testi Coffee in the renowned Sidama region. Roasted to a deeply developed medium profile, this coffee offers a rich cocoa foundation layered with notes of spiced berry compote and a lingering sweetness.

items.title: Decaf Espresso - Colombia San Antonio
items.desc: Sourced in partnership with Pergamino Exporters, this decaf brings together carefully selected washed micro-lots from San Antonio, Inzá, a region of Colombia we've been buying coffee from for nearly a decade. Rather than purchasing an already-decaffeinated coffee, we build the lot specifically for sugarcane EA decaffeination, prioritizing sweetness, balance, and clarity. We roast this coffee a bit more developed to emphasize its sweetness and body, creating an approachable, versatile decaf that performs particularly well as espresso, both on its own and with milk.

items.title: Colombia Jhoan Vergara Gesha
items.desc: Grown at 1,750 meters above sea level at Las Flores in Huila, Colombia, this washed Gesha reflects Jhoan Vergara’s meticulous approach to coffee production. Combining generations of agricultural knowledge with a deep understanding of fermentation and sensory analysis, Jhoan has established Las Flores as a source of exceptional coffees featured on competition stages around the world. This Gesha highlights his commitment to precision, clarity, and varietal expression.

items.title: Guatemala Finca Libano Gesha
items.desc: Nestled in the volcanic slopes of Guatemala’s Acatenango region, El Libano has been cultivated by the Pérez family for over a century. Grown at 1,900 meters above sea level, this Gesha reflects generations of agricultural knowledge and a continued commitment to quality under Herbert Estuardo Pérez Liquidano. Through thoughtful cultivation and a dedication to improving each harvest, El Libano has earned a reputation for producing exceptional coffees.

items.title: Panama Elida Gesha Mina Honey
items.desc: Elida Estate in Boquete, Panama has become synonymous with industry-leading quality when it comes to coffee. Winning the best of Panama and the choice of many world champions, their Gesha has literally changed the way coffee is now traded. Enjoy legendary work from true master farming, perfectly encapsulating what we expect from a washed Gesha grown in Panama.

items.title: Mexico Silvia Herrera Tupi
items.desc: In the highlands of Chiapas, Mexico, Silvia Carolina Herrera Hernandez has built a reputation for producing exceptional coffee. Her family's farm, located in Nuevo San Luis, Ocozocoautla de Espinosa, reflects a deep commitment to organic and sustainable practices, placing it at the forefront of Mexico’s growing specialty coffee movement.

items.title: Guatemala El Injerto Gesha
items.desc: Grown in the mineral-rich highlands of Huehuetenango, this washed Gesha reflects over a century of agricultural legacy at Finca El Injerto. First planted in 1900 and stewarded today by the third and fourth generations of the Aguirre family, El Injerto is a leader in sustainable, precision-driven coffee production.

items.title: Panama Kotowa Las Brujas Washed - Cafe Only
Mexico Finca Santa Cruz Gesha
items.desc: Located in the mountains of Chiapas, Mexico, Finca Santa Cruz is a family-operated farm led by José “Pepe” Argüello, a third-generation coffee producer with a remarkable commitment to quality. Situated near the biodiverse El Triunfo Biosphere Reserve, the farm has earned international recognition for its exceptional coffees, including multiple first-place finishes in Mexico's Cup of Excellence. Through careful cultivation, thoughtful processing, and a deep respect for the surrounding environment, Pepe and his family continue to produce some of Mexico's most celebrated coffees.

items.title: Colombia Altos de Quitumpamba
items.desc: From the high elevations of Nariño, this Pink Bourbon from Altos de Quitumpamba in Buesaco is grown at 2,200 meters, where altitude and volcanic soils drive intensity and clarity. Produced by Carolina Chalapud Daza and Guillermo Torres Daza, it’s a carefully washed coffee with monitored fermentation and slow raised-bed drying, resulting in a remarkably complex, high-elevation expression of Pink Bourbon.

items.title: Colombia Aponte Village Honey
items.desc: A perennial standout from the Inga producers of Aponte, this community lot from Nariño captures the highland precision and structured sweetness that have made the village a fixture in our annual sourcing. The cup is richly sweet, with a vivid red fruit note that threads through caramelized sugars. Unconventionally processed as a red honey, the coffee undergoes partial drying prior to depulping, a technique that intensifies fruit esters and lends a plush tactile to the profile.

items.title: Kenya Kagunyu AA
items.desc: Kagunyu is one of three washing stations operated by the Rumukia Farmers Cooperative Society in Nyeri, receiving coffee from roughly 600 smallholder producers farming the volcanic soils between Mt. Kenya and the Aberdare range. For this washed lot, ripe cherry is carefully sorted before depulping, fermentation, washing, and drying on raised beds, resulting in the bright acidity, clarity, and fruit character associated with coffees from this part of Kenya.

items.title: El Salvador Santa Rosa Honey
items.desc: Our relationship with Finca Santa Rosa spans more than a decade, with the last eight years shaped by an increasingly collaborative process of selection, feedback, and refinement. Raul’s precision in agronomy, processing, and lot separation allows us to cup and build our purchases from individual day lots, selecting only Pacamara coffees that meet an exceptionally high quality threshold.

items.title: GaeaStar Cups Case Pack
items.desc: Case Pack (45 cups per case)

items.title: Kenya Kamunyaka AA
items.desc: This AA seperation comes from Kamunyaka, a washing station within the Iria-Ini Farmers Cooperative Society in Kenya’s central highlands. Sitting around 1,700 meters above sea level and serving a community of smallholder producers, Kamunyaka is part of a broader effort within Iria-Ini to revitalize its stations through careful processing, experimentation, and a renewed focus on cup quality. This natural lot reflects that transformation and the station’s growing potential.

items.title: Honduras Fredy Perez
items.desc: Fredy Perez is a longtime producer in San Andrés, Lempira, and one of the people who first helped us find our footing in this relatively young coffee-producing region. Since beginning our work here around 2021, Fredy has become both a trusted producer and an important local connection, helping introduce us to neighboring farmers while continuing to push the quality of his own coffees forward.

items.title: El Salvador Santa Rosa
items.desc: This deeply sweet washed coffee from the Chalatenango Mountains comes from Finca Santa Rosa, owned and operated by our good friend Jorge Raul Rivera. Grape and rose lead the cup, opening into a layered and complex profile that has made Santa Rosa a standout in our coffee lineup.

items.title: Costa Rica Volcan Azul SL28 - Cafe Only
Ethiopia Shakiso Doyenne Natural - Cafe Only
Morning Mayhem
items.desc: Step into the ring, caffeine fiends! Magic & bird has tag teamed with Onyx Coffee Lab to slug your mouth with "Morning Mayhem"!! This coffee will suplex your sleepy taste buds and there's no tap-out. Your palate's about to get pile-driven into full-flavor submission. Brew at your own risk.

items.title: Costa Rica Las Lajas Natural
items.desc: This naturally processed coffee has become a staple in our Central American offerings and a reflection of our years working with Las Lajas. Today, they process this lot specifically for us, building a profile around the attributes we’ve come to love. Expect notes of pineapple and blueberry with a soft milk chocolate sweetness.

items.title: Panama Savage Coffees Gesha
items.desc: The Savage Coffee line is a collaboration of boutique coffee producers located in Boquete Valley and Volcan, Panama, working together to produce some of the finest coffees in the world, directly to your door. With expertise derived from generations of producers who maintain best practice techniques and a strict attention to detail from agronomy to processing. This washed Gesha variety highlights the hard work and collaborative spirit of the Savage line.

items.title: Colombia Altos de Quitumpamba Chiroso
items.desc: Following our first offering from Altos de Quitumpamba, we're excited to share this second release from Carolina Chalapud Daza and Guillermo Torres Daza, this time showcasing the remarkable Chiroso variety. Grown at 2,200 meters in the volcanic soils of Buesaco, Nariño, and processed with a meticulous washed method featuring monitored fermentation and slow raised-bed drying, the result is a coffee that balances crystalline acidity, delicate florals, and a deeply expressive sweetness.

items.title: Ecuador Jose Jijon
items.desc: This is our second release of Fincas del Putushio, a new planting from Jose Jijon. Working together with his father Pepe, they used what they had learned developing Finca El Soledad and adapted it to a high-elevation farm in a different region. Through unique challenges and trials, the effort put forth yields a tremendously clean and elegant cup.

items.title: Colombia Las Moras
items.desc: Circadian is a fully tailored coffee experience designed to optimize your caffeine intake without sacrificing sleep. Select the perfect amount of caffeine in each cup with our caffeine calculator, or buy the box set to try them all.

items.title: Decaf Colombia Sebastian Ramirez Red Fruits
items.desc: This is a unique fruit-infused decaffeinated micro-lot from our friend Sebastian Ramirez. Sebas often experiments at El Placer with the addition of fruit within the fermentation process, and this particular coffee has been co-fermented with red fruits, imparting a strong flavor of fruit throughout the drinking experience.

items.title: Colombia Nestor Lasso Ombligon - Cafes Only
items.desc: This natural processed, thermal shock Ombligon is one of the most intense coffees we have ever roasted. With layered, high sweetness, this micro-lot propelled itself to the number one spot at the WBC in 2022, and has since garnered many more accolades. We have partnered with Lohas in Colombia to bring this specially processed Ombligon, which has wowed Baristas and Consumers alike.

items.title: Decaf Colombia Inzá San Antonio - Cafes Only
items.desc: Rest easy with this washed decaffeinated coffee from Cauca, Inzá. We’ve intentionally sourced this coffee for the purpose of decaffeination, selecting this regional lot from San Antonio for it’s structured sweetness of red apple and raw sugar, with a balanced acidity reminiscent of pear.

items.title: Tropical Weather - Cafes Only
items.desc: Tropical Weather is a seasonal blend that celebrates coffees from our favorite coffee producing country: Ethiopia. We take a fresh washed offering that provides delicate florals and juicy texture, and incorporate a natural processed coffee that promotes pungent fruits and natural sugars. The result is indeed better than the sum of its parts. If you miss the long days of summer then Tropical Weather is your cup of sunshine. With a floral aroma, notes of berries and plum, along with the tannins and sweetness of sweet tea, you'll be leaving the house wearing shorts all year long.

items.title: Kaliluni AA, Kenya, Washed
items.desc: Fully washed and raised-bed dried, this mixed SL lot from Kaliluni opens with notes of red currant and bright pomegranate, with a sweet undertone of brown sugar throughout each sip.

items.title: Los Arcos, Guatemala, Washed
items.desc: A crisp, comforting Washed coffee from the eastern highlands of Jalapa. Bright red apple leads into the dark, jammy sweetness of raisin, carried by a structured black tea body and a clean, lingering finish.

items.title: El Árbol, Nicaragua, CM Natural Jasper
items.desc: Pineapple, orange and chocolate

items.title: Trifle
items.desc: Vanilla custard, brandy (0% alcohol) and baked stonefruit

items.title: Kiambu Regional PB, Kenya, Washed
items.desc: A Peaberry selection from Kiambu's Washed regional lots, where the coffee delivers a concentrated, juicy cup of fresh plum and raisin over a sweet toffee finish.

items.title: Thageini Lot 2226, Kenya, CM Washed Indigo
items.desc: Mandarin, caramel and lavender 200g

items.title: Guji Mudole, Ethiopia, Supernatural
items.desc: Tropical, red berries and concord grape 200g

items.title: La Huerta, Honduras, Washed
items.desc: A bright, floral Washed Catimor from the slopes of Santa Barbara Mountain. Soft botanical notes give way to red apple, rounding out with a gentle walnut finish.

items.title: Yirgacheffe Gelcha Kindu Lot 1426, Ethiopia, CM Natural Indigo
items.desc: Malt, blueberry and raisin

items.title: Kuriru AB, Kenya, Washed
items.desc: Currant, grapefruit and green tea

items.title: La Merced, Guatemala, Natural
items.desc: A juicy, balanced natural Bourbon from one of Guatemala's most storied family farms. Ripe yellow plum and sweet cherry open into bright strawberry jam, settling into a rich dark chocolate finish that keeps every sip round and generous.

items.title: Los Pirineos Lot 07, El Salvador, Natural
items.desc: A classic high-grown Bourbon given a slow, careful natural dry, Lot 07 opens with ripe apricot over a sweet botanical base, settling into a chamomile finish.

items.title: Raspberry Candy
items.desc: Inspired by the coffee used by ONA Coffee founder, Saša Śestić in his winning routine at the 2015 World Barista Championship, Raspberry Candy has become a favourite in the coffee industry for its playful fruit notes and indulgent sweetness. This long-awaited filter release of Raspberry Candy captures those same fruit-forward flavours in a black coffee experience. With layers of Ethiopian coffees and a delicate roast profile, it highlights the unmistakable raspberry candy character alongside a deep, rich chocolate and a floral, hibiscus-like finish.

items.title: Unwind
items.desc: Enjoy all the flavour without the caffeine. Unwind by ONA Coffee is a smooth, balanced decaf coffee blend—perfect for espresso or milk-based drinks.

items.title: Maple
items.desc: The maple tree's enduring strength speaks to our commitment to nature and sustainability. Maple was created to be a traditional style milk coffee, perfect for everyday drinking. It is a bold, full-bodied coffee with flavours of caramel, malt, nut and spices.

items.title: Gateway
items.desc: Want an approachable introduction to specialty coffee? If you’re new to coffee or buying beans for someone just starting their journey, our Gateway Coffee is the perfect milk-based coffee blend to ease you in. These coffee beans deliver a sweet, creamy profile with tasting notes of chocolate truffle and mixed berries.

items.title: Aspen
items.desc: An Aspen is a variety of poplar tree that reminds us of where ONA first started. Throwing back to the memories that founder Saša Šestić has of Canberra's poplar-lined roads, as he travelled from roastery to cafe. This full-flavoured blend is decadent and smooth, designed for everyday drinking. It is the perfect coffee for chocolate lovers.

items.title: Haro Wachu

Expect notes of blueberry, lemon curd, and floral honey, coming together in a beautifully balanced cup. A great choice for anyone looking to explore the fruity and floral side of Ethiopian coffee.

Intense, complex, and wonderfully expressive, this is a truly experimental Wush Wush that leaves a lasting impression. Available for both filter and espresso.

In the cup, expect delicate notes of yellow plum, fig, and Earl Grey, complemented by a vibrant yet rounded mouthfeel and a beautifully refined sweetness. A coffee created to stand apart — now available for you to experience. Enjoy it as filter or espresso.

items.desc: We’re excited to share another delicious coffee from Rwanda! These washed Red Bourbon coffeebeans, is grown in the high mountains at an elevation of 1,850 to 2,300 meters above sea level. items.title: Ruronzi

After fermentation, the cherries are slowly dried on raised beds to preserve the complex aromatic compounds developed during processing. The result is a vibrant and expressive coffee with intense fruit aromatics, refined sweetness, and a clean, well-structured cup. Expect blueberry, melon, and cherry with a juicy mouthfeel in your cup!

As a competition coffee, it boasts remarkable character and is now available for you to enjoy. In the cup, you will find notes of rose lemonade, orange, and papaya, balanced by a vibrant, juicy mouthfeel and refined sweetness. Experience it now as either a filter coffee or an espresso.

In the cup, expect a memorable profile of yellow raspberry, rose, and bergamot, combining juicy sweetness with delicate florals and a refined citrus lift. items.title: Los Mendoza [Geisha 2F Washed]
items.desc: Un Geisha tout en finesse, où l’élégance rencontre la complexité. Dès les premières gorgées, le kumquat apporte une fraîcheur zestée et délicatement acidulée, rapidement rejoint par la douceur veloutée de la pêche. En fond de tasse, le thé noir vient prolonger la dégustation avec une belle profondeur, une touche tannique et une finale tout en délicatesse. Un café lumineux et raffiné, où les notes fruitées s’entrelacent avec la subtilité des arômes de thé. Une tasse précise, élégante et pleine de nuances, qui invite à prendre son temps.

items.title: Alo Bekele Bute [240h Fermentation Washed]
items.desc: Direction l’Éthiopie, berceau historique du café, avec ce lot signé Alo qui met en lumière toute la finesse et l’expressivité du terroir éthiopien. Issu d’une fermentation lavée prolongée de 240 heures, ce café développe une tasse élégante et lumineuse, où la délicatesse florale du chèvrefeuille rencontre la fraîcheur zestée du citron. À mesure que la dégustation évolue, la papaye apporte une touche exotique et juteuse, tandis que la mûre vient prolonger l’expérience avec une belle profondeur fruitée. Un café tout en contraste et en équilibre, entre éclat, douceur florale et gourmandise fruité

items.title: Finca El Destino [Duende GW6]

items.title: Finca Milan [Spice Kaza Triple Process]
items.desc: Un café vibrant et gourmand, où la douceur exotique rencontre une belle complexité aromatique. L’orange sanguine apporte ensuite une fraîcheur acidulée et une jolie vivacité, tandis que la noix de coco vient arrondir l’ensemble avec une douceur crémeuse et exotique. items.desc: La ferme Arara est une mini parcelle appartenant à Assefa et Multugeta Dukamo. Une belle explosion de fruits, entre douceur tropicale, fraîcheur acidulée et gourmandise, qui offre une dégustation aussi vibrante qu’élégante. Un café lumineux et généreux, idéal pour les amateurs de profils fruités et exotiques.

DIGS parcourt les terroirs les plus réputés à la recherche des meilleurs micro-lots. items.title: CGLE Cerro Azul [Geisha Hybrid Washed]
items.desc: Issu de la légendaire Granja La Esperanza, ce Geisha d’exception est cultivé à une altitude comprise entre 1 700 et 1 900 mètres, sur les pentes fertiles de la ferme Cerro Azul, dans la région de Valle del Cauca. items.title: Finca Capri [Chiroso Washed]

items.desc: Un café qui a du caractère tout en restant élégant. La dégustation commence par une attaque vive, où le thé noir rencontre l’acidité délicate de la rhubarbe. items.title: Alo [Sky Project FL]
items.desc: Issu du Sky Project d’Alo Coffee, ce lot pousse dans le village d’Alo, à Bensa. L’idée du projet est aussi simple que radicale : aller chercher des altitudes où les nuits plus fraîches ralentissent la maturation des cerises. Une maturation plus lente permet aux fruits d’accumuler davantage de sucres et de développer une expression aromatique particulièrement dense. En tasse, le café joue sur la carte du fruit et de la fraîcheur. La pêche apparaît d’abord : pulpeuse, mûre, juteuse. Puis arrive le raisin rouge et sa sucrosité éclatante. Enfin, se dévoile la groseille avec son acidité vive.

items.title: Finca Rosma [Geisha Washed]
items.desc: Un Geisha lavé tout en finesse, issu de la Finca Rosma à Huehuetenango. Cette ferme familiale, fondée en 1963 par Alejandro Morales est aujourd’hui dirigée par la famille Morales. La tasse s’ouvrira sur des notes délicates de jasmin et de citron, amenant une acidité élégante. Puis, le café gagnera en douceur, des notes d’abricot sucrés accompagnées d’une texture soyeuse évoquant le lait d’amande. Un café équilibré, floral et lumineux.

items.title: Alo [Zero Fermentation Washed]
items.desc: Derrière ce Zero Fermentation Washed, Alo cherche à retirer une étape devenue presque incontournable dans les lavés modernes : la fermentation. Les cerises mûres sont triées, dépulpées puis lavées immédiatement, sans passage en cuves. L’objectif, simple en apparence est très exigeant en pratique, il faut éviter que la fermentation ne façonne le profil aromatique et laisser la variété et le terroir s’exprimer avec le moins d’interférences possibles. items.title: Elto [Elora RF8 Natural]

Pour notre lot RF8 Naturel, les cerises fermentent naturellement dans des sacs hermétiques immergés dans une rivière, avant un séchage lent permettant de préserver la richesse aromatique développée pendant le processus. C’est entre 1200 et 1550 mètres d’altitude que la ferme cultive différentes variétés d’arabica, dont le Geisha. Santa Elena est aujourd’hui porté par la famille Ameglio, dont l’histoire agricole au Panama remonte à plusieurs générations. Ce Caturra Lavé de Jamison Savage en fait partie. La tasse commence sur quelque chose de gourmand : le chocolat au lait, puis arrive la prune rouge, avec cette sensation vive et élégante que l’on retrouve dans les cafés kenyans. Une grande partie de son territoire reste couverte de forêt, et les plantations de café occupent notamment les secteurs plus élévés. Graciano Cruz a une approche construite autour des procédés classiques de traitement, avec une volonté de travailler le café sans chercher à le rendre artificiellement spectaculaire. Le nom Lino ne désigne pas une variété, mais un bien lot spécifique de la ferme, en isolant des parcelles précises, Hacienda la Esmeralda vient chercher à isoler les expressions les plus intéressantes du terroir. items.desc: Sur les hauts plateaux de Bensa, en Éthiopie, se trouve Elto Coffee, projet d’Eliyas Dukamo et d’Atiklit Dejene. items.desc: Issu de mythique terroir de Gesha Village, au coeur de la région de West Omo en Éthiopie, ce lot Oma G26 E24 est cultivé sur les pentes du bloc Oma, où la variété Gesha 1931 exprime tpute sa finesse. Le coquelicot vient évoquer une douceur florale, rejoint par une myrtille juteuse et l’orange vient ensuite illuminer l’ensemble d’une fraîcheur vive, laissant une finale longue et élégante. Chaque tasse évoluera en refroidissant, dé

items.desc: Découvrez ce magnifique lot 121 Geisha lavé issue de la plantation Hacienda Janson. Il se dévoilera en tasse un café expressif et pur, caractéristique des hauts plateaux de la région de Chiriqui, au Panama, nichée sur les hauts plateaux de Volcan. items.title: Alo Bore [Washed]
items.desc: Ce lot vient des hauteurs du Guji, en Éthiopie, où Tamiru Tadesse cultive la variété 74158 à plus de 2000 mètres d’altitude. Traité en lavé, il offre une tasse nette et florale, où les fleurs blanches laissent place à la pêche, avant une finale vive de pamplemousse.

items.title: Little Orange
items.desc: Our latest Ethiopian from Danche in Gedeo is a natural, and a particularly fun one! We taste orange candy, honeycomb & mango in a bright, juicy cup with that clean finish we love from Ethiopian coffees. Delicate on filter, and our favourite at the last cupping.

items.title: Choco Nuts
items.desc: Choco Nuts is our latest Brazilian espresso, produced by Adriano Muñiz and his family at Agropecuária Muñiz in Sul de Minas. This anaerobic natural Catucaí has everything we enjoy in a classic Brazilian coffee, with plenty of sweetness, a round body and a creamy texture. Expect notes of hazelnut, milk chocolate and vanilla, making it a great everyday espresso that also works really well with milk.

items.title: Pillow Talk
items.desc: Los Nogales does decaf a little differently. This Caturra is grown, processed and decaffeinated at the farm in Pitalito, giving Oscar Hernandez and his team control over the coffee from cherry to finished decaf. It’s bright and sweet, with starfruit, agave and rosemary. A decaf we’d happily drink whether we were looking for one or not. * Due to the decaffeination process, the beans may have an unusual colour. This is completely normal and does not affect the quality of the coffee.

items.title: Peachy Daze
items.desc: Peachy Daze is back, a clean washed Ethiopian from the Chelbesa washing station in Gedeb, where heirloom varieties grow at 2173 masl. The cup is light and delicate, with white peach and lemon up front, black tea through the middle and a soft elderflower finish.

items.title: Blackberry Dust
items.desc: Blackberry Dust is a late-harvest natural Ethiopian coffee from the Buku Abel washing station in Guji, which arrived in Europe just a few weeks ago. Around 400 smallholder farmers contribute to the station, growing heirloom varieties at elevations between 1,900 and 2,100 masl. The cup is fruity and sweet, with notes of blackberry, wild strawberry and blueberry yoghurt, followed by a soft, creamy finish.

items.title: Macaron
items.desc: One of our all-time favourites from Johan and Diego Vergara at Las Flores, this natural Red Bourbon has become one of those coffees we’re always excited to bring back. It goes through an advanced anaerobic natural process and comes out big, juicy and seriously sweet, with strawberry jam, raspberry macaron and buttercream.

items.title: Sticky Pudding
items.desc: Our Christmas coffee is here! This year we’ve worked with CATA Export in Colombia to create something inspired by the festive season. This bourbon undergoes a co-fermentation with cinnamon, cardamom, mandarin and cherry, giving it a distinctive profile while keeping plenty of sweetness in the cup. Expect notes of cinnamon, cardamom and fresh fir – a very festive profile.

items.title: Cream Donut
items.desc: Cream Donut is a collaboration with Cata Export and producer Franky Hoyos in Colombia. A yeast-inoculated natural Caturra Chiroso developed for DAK through rounds of back-and-forth trialling. It’s an unusual coffee that has somehow become one of our staples and a bestseller, loved for its distinct character and the ridiculously good flat white it makes. Expect chocolate milk, cherry-filled doughnut and vanilla, whether you brew it as filter or espresso.

items.title: Milky Cake
items.desc: Milky Cake has been with us since 2021 and has become one of our bestsellers. Originally developed with Cata Export and Diego Samuel Bermudez at Finca El Paraíso in Colombia, it’s an advanced anaerobic washed Castillo with a profile that’s hard to mistake for anything else. Vanilla cake, pistachio, cardamom and honey, with a creamy sweetness that works as filter, espresso or with milk.

items.title: Plum Butter
items.desc: Plum Butter is a natural from Bulambuli in East Uganda, produced with our long-time partners at Ibero. It’s a profile we don’t come across often from Uganda: deep, smooth and fruit-forward, with dark plum, grape cordial and cacao. Rich without becoming too heavy.

items.title: Berry Blues
items.desc: Berry Blues is back. We’ve had this coffee in different variations over the years, sometimes under Berry Blues, sometimes as Blueberry Boom, and it remains a favourite across the DAK team for its big fruit character and how much fun it is to drink. This year’s harvest from Esayas Beriso is an anaerobic natural, grown high in Oromia, Ethiopia, and slowly dried in the shade. There’s plenty of dark fruit and a boozy edge: grape soda up front, myrtle liquor behind it, and a cashew-butter richness that gives the cup its buttery body and creamy mouthfeel.

items.title: Darling
items.desc: Darling comes from Danche Washing Station in Gedeb, and it’s one of the more delicate Ethiopians we’ve had this year. The coffee goes through a 48-hour anaerobic fermentation before being washed, resulting in a cup with good clarity despite the additional fermentation. Wild florals lead, followed by peach iced tea and a black-tea finish. Light, elegant and very tea-like.

items.title: Rhubarb Fizz
items.desc: Our next Kenyan of the season, and one of our favourites this year. Rhubarb Fizz is a washed AA from Ndimi Factory in Kirinyaga, bringing together SL28, SL34, Batian and Ruiru 11 from the surrounding smallholder farms. Juicy and layered, with rhubarb soda, blackcurrant and orange.

items.title: Hazel Nuts
items.desc: Hazel Nuts is a natural Catuaí from Chinacla in the Marcala region of Honduras, grown by our longtime partners Marysabel Caballero and Moises Herrera. We’ve been buying their coffees for years, and this is one we particularly like for espresso. Round and silky, with hazelnut, cacao nibs and blackberry, plus a touch of booziness that we really enjoy. Especially good with milk.

items.title: Silky Way
items.desc: Silky Way is another coffee from Jhoan and Diego Vergara at Las Flores, the same family behind Macaron. This time it’s their washed Pink Bourbon, with a completely different side of the farm showing up in the cup. Lemongrass, white florals and crisp green apple, with a bright, sparkling quality that suits the name pretty well.

items.title: The Alchemist
items.desc: The Alchemist is one of the staples in our line-up and a coffee we source directly from Gasharu Farms in Nyamasheke, Rwanda. An anaerobic natural Red Bourbon that changes quite a bit depending on how you brew it. Espresso pushes the cacao forward; filter opens up the tropical fruit and jammy sweetness. Complex, rich and particularly good with milk.

items.title: Jazz fruits
items.desc: Jazz Fruits is a staple in our lineup and one we try to keep around all year, whenever the harvest allows. We source this community lot from Daye Bensa each year for its fruity, easy-going profile and how well it works as espresso, especially with milk. Strawberry, white chocolate and mandarin in the cup. Named after the Jazz Fruits playlists on Spotify.

items.title: Mucho Berry Blend
items.desc: Mucho Berry Momos Coffee’s fourth signature blend Ethiopia is widely known as one of the coffee-growing regions loved by many people. In particular, Ethiopian coffees processed by the natural method are recognized for their diverse berry-like aromas and their broad appeal, making them enjoyable for a wide range of drinkers. Inspired by these berry characteristics, the fourth signature blend, Mucho Berry, was created to express rich and attractive berry-forward aromas.

items.title: Fruity Bonbon Blend
items.desc: Fruity Bonbon Momos Coffee’s second signature blend In 2009, when specialty coffee was first encountered in the United States, coffees with bright acidity and fruit-like aromas were still unfamiliar to many people. However, drawn to the diverse aromas and new flavors found in high-quality coffee, Momos Coffee introduced its second signature blend, Fruity Bonbon, to share the distinct character and appeal of specialty coffee.

items.title: Es Chocolat Blend
items.desc: Es Chocolat Momos Coffee’s first signature blend Es Chocolat, the very first signature blend introduced by Momos Coffee, was developed at a time when dark-roasted coffees reminiscent of chocolate were the mainstream style. It reflects the early days of Momos Coffee and the intention to create a coffee that could be enjoyed and loved by everyone.

items.title: Decaf Beans
items.desc: A quality washed Red Bourbon from Rwanda. It has preserved the pleasant stewed fruit and spice notes associated with Rwandan coffee. This is the first time we have launched a Rwandan decaffeinated coffee. Like the Ethiopian decaf that we launched earlier this year, this coffee nicely displays the character of its origin.

items.title: SOLO
items.desc: SOLO is a seasonal single-origin washed coffee offering a molasses sweetness, gentle berry acidity and a syrupy body that carries through to a great finish. In the highlands of western Guatemala, smallholder producers in Huehuetenango farm steep, fertile slopes where coffee sustains much of the local economy. Working collectively through the Regional Select programme, they’ve built a system that rewards quality while keeping value close to origin. This lot was crafted to capture the essence of Huehuetenango's flavour.

items.title: Foundation Beans
items.desc: A great example of Costa Rican coffee offering rounded sweetness, mellow acidity and a full mouthfeel. This coffee is brought to us by Cafe Imports, whose sourcing programme in Costa Rica is centred around Oxcart Coffee, their local import-export operation. Oxcart aims to work with the same micromills year after year, building lasting relationships. Beyond its commercial role, Oxcart also acts as a resource for the local coffee community by promoting candid conversations about quality and production. items.title: Rare Beans
items.desc: A classic Ethiopian natural profile offering rich, ripe fruit notes reminiscent of blueberries. Gara Agena sits on a steep hillside at approximately 2,250 MASL, with the Geta River wrapping around the site. This location was not chosen by accident: it offers ideal elevation, growing conditions and access to clean water. The site is overseen by Mr Faysel A. Yonis, the owner of Testi Coffee. items.title: Gesha Beans
items.desc: A floral washed Gesha with fruity sweetness and a tea-like finish. items.title: Familia Toledo Ortiz - Washed Process - 2026
items.desc: This lot comes from the combined harvests of father-and-son producers Edernoman Toledo Charry and Yoan Arley Toledo, who shared this coffee with us under their family name, Toledo Ortiz. Both Edernoman and Yoan were responsible for some of our favorite coffees of 2026, and we’re excited to be closing out the year with an outstanding pink bourbon variety separation that they produced together on their family farm, Finca Los Andes. As two of the most exciting talents to emerge from our longstanding Divino Niño partnership in recent years, we can’t wait to see what the future holds for these two.

items.title: La Tortuga - Washed Process - Education Lot - 2025
items.desc: After a brief hiatus, we're delighted to welcome back La Tortuga, one of Passenger’s original Education Lot menu favorites. This community blend, produced by an association of small coffee farmers on the Galápagos Islands, offers a fascinating example of the impact of unique microclimates on specialty coffee production. While produced at elevations far below what is typically considered appropriate for specialty coffee production, this coffee defies expectations thanks to the fortuitous environmental impact of the Humboldt Current. In the cup, we find aromatics of marzipan and browning sugar,

items.title: William Abad - Washed Process - 2025
items.desc: This mejorado variety separation comes from producer William Abad’s farm, El Pino, located in Ecuador’s Zamora region. While most of our sourcing in Ecuador has focused on the Pichincha region in the north-central part of the country, we’ve occasionally featured exceptional producers from Zamora as well. Zamora is located nearly three hundred miles southeast of the Pichincha region near the Amazon basin, and close to neighboring Peru. The area's proximity to the Amazon rainforest creates a more humid and tropical environment compared to the mountainous terrain of Pichincha, perhaps contributin

items.title: Finca Perla Negra - Washed Process - 2025
items.desc: Perla Negra is an award-winning farm in Pichincha, Ecuador, run by Olger Rogel and Magda Zabala alongside their daughter, Nanci Rogel. Known for their exploration of unconventional coffee genetics, the family grows a diverse collection of varieties and unique selections. This particular lot is composed of a variety that Olger calls ‘Lupe Maria.’ Although its provenance has yet to be confirmed through genetic testing, its morphology bears some resemblance to Coffea eugenioides , a species also cultivated on the farm and one of the ancestral species of Arabica. In the cup we find many of the hal

items.title: Silvio Leite - Natural Process - 2023
items.desc: Benefiting from its proximity to the Chapada Diamantina mountain range, the Piatã municipality in Brazil’s Bahia region is home to some of the most celebrated coffees in the country. This dry processed lot from legendary producer Silvio Leite in Piatã was awarded second place among a collection of his auction lot coffees from the 2022 harvest year. Kept in freezer preservation since its arrival to our warehouse in early 2023, we're delighted to share the very last of this Reserve Lot as one final archival release for the year. We've been finding nuanced aromatics of floral honey and orange pee

items.title: 2026 Holiday Coffee & Herbal Blend
items.desc: Why choose between coffee and tea? The more the merrier is what we say! This bundle features a 250 gram bag of Holiday Coffee and a 50 gram tube of Holiday Herbal.

items.title: Holiday Coffee - Washed Process - 2026
items.desc: This year’s Holiday Coffee features a selection from our newest Foundational Partnership, Thamani, in Kenya. This washed Kamathura lot, sourced through our partners at Kamavindi Coffee Labs, brings together coffees from two distinct cooperative societies: Gichathaini Factory and Murarandia Factory. In the cup, we find a festive array of seasonal flavors, including notes of spiced plum and cranberry complemented by bright orange zest and a comforting chocolate finish.

items.title: Necessary Holiday Blend 2026
items.desc: This rich and comforting blend has balanced notes of warming spices, toffee, and dark chocolate, making it the perfect cup for sharing with loved ones, fueling traditions old and new, and enjoying all throughout the season.

items.title: Kerehaklu Peaberry - Washed Process - 2026
items.desc: This peaberry lot comes from a small selection of early outturns from the 2025–26 harvest at Kerehaklu Estate. The Selection 9 variety featured in this lot ripens earlier than many of the other varieties common to the area, and the small size of peaberries requires specialized milling equipment. As a result, Pranoy chose to mill these lots separately and earlier in the harvest cycle. Many of these peaberry lots remained in-country, finding their way onto the menus of some of India’s most celebrated specialty roasters. When we visited Kerehaklu earlier this year, however, Pranoy mentioned a sep

items.title: Kerehaklu - Washed Process - 2026
items.desc: This selection from the 2025–26 harvest at Kerehaklu Estate in Chikmagalur, India, features what producer Pranoy Thipiah describes as an Extended Mosto Washed process. It begins with the creation of a ‘mosto,’ made from a mix of parchment coffee and coffee cherry mucilage that creates a starter culture from the active native yeasts and bacteria present on the remaining fruit. Cherries selected for processing then undergo an initial overnight, open-air fermentation in whole cherry before being pulped and fermented again in lidded barrels containing a mixture of water and the prepared starter cu

items.title: Kerehaklu - Natural Process - 2026
items.desc: When producer Pranoy Thipiah invited us into his quality lab outside Kerehaklu Estate's processing site earlier this year, we couldn’t help but notice something intriguing: a small, lidded barrel filled with whole coffee cherries and a pink-hued liquid, with an aquarium bubbler slowly adding oxygen to the mixture. As it turns out, this small experiment would lead to a massive cup profile when scaled up. It's what Pranoy calls his Oxygenated Cascara Mosto Natural. As with many of Pranoy’s coffees, the process begins with the creation of a ‘mosto’ - a type of starter culture made by allowing cof

items.title: Thamani
items.desc: The most recent addition to the Foundational Menu, this vibrant field blend features the renowned SL28 and SL34 varieties. While Thamani may be sourced from other producer partners in the years to come, this inaugural expression was produced at Kamavindi Estate by our dear friends the Mbature family.

items.title: Kambarare - Washed Process - 2025
items.desc: Last year marked our first time purchasing coffee from Gerald Njagi, a third generation coffee producer and manager of Kambarare Estate in Kirinyaga County in Kenya. Through continued collaboration with the Mbature family and their export operations at Kamavindi Coffee Lab, we are delighted to be able to feature another outstanding washed SL variety lot from the most recent harvest at Kambarare. Again this year, the quality of Gerald's single variety SL separations stood out on the cupping table for their refined flavor complexity, and notable depth of sweetness. This particular lot of SL vari

items.title: Bumba - Washed Process - 2025
items.desc: This Reserve Lot selection is one of two coffees in our most recent release featuring lots processed at the Long Miles Ninga washing station. Run by meticulous station manager Agathon Ininahazwe, Ninga station is capable of producing extraordinary washed and honey-processed coffees. This particular washed lot is made up of small harvests from producers from nearby Bumba hill in Kayanza province. A classic Burundi profile, we’re tasting dark dried fruit and breakfast tea in the cup, alongside mild orange acidity and spiced chocolate in the finish.

items.title: Luz Mary Hurtado - Washed Process - 2025
items.desc: Luz Mary Hurtado is one of a growing number of award-winning coffee producers we've had the privilege of discovering through our long-standing Divino Niño partnership in the municipality of Suaza in Central Huila. Last fall, Luz placed among the top twenty producers in the Central Region category of the annual Copa de Oro competition, and her exceptional talent is once again on display in this impressively sweet and nuanced field blend of pink bourbon and gesha varieties. A fitting expression of the plant genetics at play, we taste classic pink bourbon characteristics of sweet dark berries and

items.title: Abdo Aba Mecha - EA Decaf - Education Lot - 2025
items.desc: This decaf Education Lot is a blend of washed and natural processed lots from the 30 hectare estate of producer Abdo Aba Mecha. Abdo began working with our import partners at Osito back in 2023, around the same time that we featured a natural processed lot from one of Abdo’s neighbors, Nesru Abanura. This area, in Ethiopia’s western Jimma Zone, is close to many of of the producers we work closely with for our Agaro Foundational partnership, so we’ve been delighted to see it continue to develop as a hub for talented, quality-driven producers. We selected this lot as a candidate for the Educatio

items.title: Fausto Romo Sidra - Washed Process - 2025
items.desc: Released alongside a honey processed lot from the 2025 harvest at La Carolina in Pichincha, Ecuador, this washed processed sidra variety separation from producer Fausto Romo exemplifies why sidra has become synonymous with specialty coffees from Ecuador. In the cup we taste vibrant white grape, subtle florals, and an integrated panela-like sweetness, followed by a finish of soft pome fruit reminiscent of pear and yellow apple.

items.title: Wilmer Julca - Washed Process - 2025
items.desc: Now in our second consecutive year working with producer Wilmer Julca, this selection from his 2025 harvest exemplifies the outstanding quality potential of coffees grown at extremely high elevations in the celebrated coffee producing region of Cajamarca, Peru. In the cup we find a deeply sweet and savory quality reminiscent of molasses, cooked fruit, and spiced orange.

items.title: Abel Raymundo Arotaype - Washed Process - Cup of Excellence - 2024
items.desc: It’s no exaggeration to say that the Abel Raymundo Arotaype Huayllas is among the highest elevation coffee producers in the world. Located at nearly 2500 masl, his farm, El Pedregal, is located in the west of Cusco near the border with the neighboring Ayacucho department. This past year we’ve tasted a number of outstanding geshas from this region, so it was no surprise to see this coffee given due acclaim at the 2024 Peru Cup of Excellence, where it was awarded 11th place overall.

items.title: Familia Morales Rivera - Washed Process - Cup of Excellence - 2022
items.desc: Carefully preserved since arriving at our freezer facility in the spring of 2023, this coffee continues to be among the highest-scoring coffees ever to come across Passenger’s cupping table. Simply put, its cup profile possesses a level of refinement and complexity that we rarely encounter from coffees anywhere in the world. Awarded third place in the 2022 Ecuador Cup of Excellence competition, it's an immaculate expression of the Sidra and Mejorado varieties from the Rivera family farm in Pichincha, Ecuador, providing a glimpse into the extraordinary potential of Ecuador’s signature plant gen

items.title: Daterra Aramosa - Natural - Education Lot - 2024
items.desc: The Aramosa ‘pre-cultivar’ featured in this Education Lot is the result of a unique hybridization between two distinct species of the Coffea genus: Arabica and Racemosa. The result is a more drought tolerant and pest resistant plant that exhibits a vibrant cup character and a naturally lower-caffeine content. As with the majority of the natural process lots from Daterra, cherries for this lot were ‘dried on tree’ before being harvested and sorted. This cup has many of the fruit-forward flavors we’ve come to expect from these unique plant genetics: Plum and fruit taffy flavors with an herbal fl

items.title: Daterra Catuai SH3 - Natural - Education Lot - 2024
items.desc: The catuai SH3 cultivar featured in this Education Lot selection from Daterra offers a case study in how coffee producers and research institutions around the world are working together to combat the effects of climate change on coffee production through careful study of coffee plant genetics and the development of new more climate resilient varieties. As with the majority of the natural process lots from Daterra, cherries for this lot were fully ‘dried on tree’ before being harvested and sorted. In the cup we find a notable Meyer lemon acidity, balanced by flavors of praline and dark chocolat

items.title: Necessary India
items.desc: A bold, grounding blend of arabica and robusta from Passenger’s Bhadra partnership. This coffee brings together rich notes of dark chocolate and toasted sesame, with a smooth intensity that’s perfect for everyday drinking.

items.title: Bhadra
items.desc: This delightfully sweet and approachable coffee comes from a small group of family-run coffee farms that together make up the Bhadra partnership. All of these estates are located near the Bhadra Tiger Reserve, in the historically significant coffee-growing region of Chikmagalur, India.

items.title: Necessary Decaf
items.desc: The rich, malted chocolate and maple syrup qualities of this incredibly sweet decaffeinated coffee from Colombia prove that no decaf drinker should ever need to compromise on flavor.

items.title: Los Sueños - Decaf
items.desc: Our Los Sueños Decaf is comprised of community lots from our producer partners in Divino Niño. These lots are Ethyl Acetate decaffeinated in Colombia before heading directly to our freezer storage facility in Lancaster.

items.title: Stowaway
items.desc: Comprised of coffees from three Foundational Partnerships, Montecarlos, Agaro, and Cusco, Stowaway is an incredibly balanced and widely approachable blend that has served as the mainstay espresso offering at Passenger's flagship King St. café in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, since our beginnings.

items.title: Divino Niño
items.desc: Centrally located in the celebrated producing region of Huila, producers near the small hamlet of Divino Niño produce this outstanding community blend that exemplifies the hallmark flavors of a classic Colombian coffee.

items.title: Necessary Dark
items.desc: With comforting flavors of bittersweet chocolate and graham cracker, this classic Dark Roast tastes great on its own or with the addition of cream and sugar.

items.title: Necessary Ethiopia
items.desc: The hallmark qualities of Ethiopian coffee abound in this refreshing and balanced cup, with flavors of stone fruit, florals, and a sweet toffee-like finish.

items.title: Necessary Burundi
items.desc: Dark berries, subtle warming spices, and a molasses-like sweetness come together in this quintessential Burundi selection.

items.title: Heza
items.desc: Highlighting the exceptional work of the Long Miles Coffee Project, the complex and unique flavor profile of Burundian coffee is on full display in this Foundational offering comprised of coffees processed at the Heza washing station.

items.title: Montecarlos
items.desc: This rich and inviting Foundational offering comes from visionary fifth-generation coffee producer Carlos Batres and his wife Julie, who have remained steadfast and pioneering stewards of the Montecarlos Estate since the 1980's

items.title: Cusco
items.desc: Passenger’s Cusco partnership reflects a commitment to supporting coffee farming communities in Peru by fostering sustainably-focused growth and delivering exceptional, consistent coffees to customers year after year.

items.title: Keystone
items.desc: This dynamic blend of coffees from our Divino Niño and Agaro partnerships is roasted to highlight clear origin flavors that combine to create a uniquely delicious offering applicable to a wide array of brewing applications.

items.title: Necessary Colombia
items.desc: This classic Colombian profile delivers deeply satisfying candied nut and milk chocolate sweetness alongside subtle flavors of cooked red fruit.

items.title: Necessary Blend
items.desc: This enticing, easy-drinking blend of Colombian and Ethiopian coffees offers a harmonious balance of chocolate, brown sugar, and just a touch of fruit.

items.title: Agaro
items.desc: Showcasing the rich heritage of Ethiopian coffee, this offering is sourced in partnership with Addis Exporter, reflecting a steadfast commitment to quality and transparency in every cup.

items.title: DR Congo — Tumaini Coffee Co-Op
items.desc: DR Congo — Tumaini Coffee Co-Op The cherries are naturally processed and dried on raised beds at Tumaini’s collection centres, where access to running water can be limited. Assembly helped fund several of these drying beds during our first year working with the cooperative, allowing producers to dry their lots locally. Drying the cherries whole helps retain their natural sweetness, resulting in a rich, rounded cup with a smooth finish.

items.title: Peru — Mikan
items.desc: Peru — Mikan Grown in the high-altitude areas around Jaén, this coffee benefits from a humid high-jungle climate, rich volcanic soils and plenty of tropical rainfall. Ripe cherries are hand-picked and processed on the smallholder producers’ individual farms using hand-pulping machines, before being fermented in tanks and dried on patios or raised beds. Once processed all lots are sent to Falcon’s production facility, Mikan, in Jaén. The washed process keeps things clean and balanced, highlighting the Tabi variety’s characteristic sweetness, citrus acidity and smooth body. Expect orange and van

items.title: Colombia — Cata Reserva Year 2
items.desc: Colombia — Cata Reserva Year 2 Grown on a sunlit 4.5-acre plot of mature Castillo trees, this lot was selectively hand-sorted before processing. Ripe cherries underwent 2–3 days of open-tank oxidation. The cherries were then pulped to remove the mucilage, before undergoing four days of sealed fermentation with coffee mosto – sugars from previous fermentations – and panela, an unrefined whole cane sugar. This controlled approach encourages a thorough fermentation while avoiding unwanted alcohol-like flavours.

items.title: Colombia — Maria Rodriguez
items.desc: Colombia — Maria Rodriguez This SL28 is naturally processed, with a 48-hour anaerobic fermentation playing a key role in developing its depth of flavour. Ripe cherries are harvested, floated and sorted before being placed in sealed tanks, where the controlled fermentation builds richer fruit character while retaining SL28’s signature clean profile. The cherries are then slowly sun-dried on raised beds for 20–30 days, turned regularly to ensure even dehydration and prevent over-fermentation. items.title: Rwanda — Jonathan Ngoga Year 2
items.desc: Rwanda — Jonathan Ngoga Year 2 Cherries from Jonathan’s farm are processed as a dedicated single-producer lot at Muraho Trading Company’s Rugali washing station, alongside coffees from the surrounding smallholder community. The cherries are hand-sorted before being floated and pulped, with underripe or damaged fruit removed at each stage. The coffee is then fermented for around 12 hours in concrete tanks, with the parchment agitated several times throughout the process. After fermentation, it is washed and graded by density before being hand-sorted again and laid out to dry for around 30 days.

items.title: Tanzania — Edelweiss Estate Kent
items.desc: Tanzania — Edelweiss Estate Kent Selected at Doddengooda Estate in Mysore, India, Kent KP9293 was originally prized for its resistance to coffee leaf rust, while retaining the classic sweetness associated with the Typica varietal. Whole cherries are pre-fermented for 24 hours beneath black tarpaulins to enhance sweetness and body before drying slowly in the sun over 25-26 days. Dried coffee is then transferred to hermetic storage until milling. The result is a silky smooth cup, full of ripe stone fruits and a boozy richness.

items.title: Guatemala — Santa Irene Catuaí
items.desc: Guatemala — Santa Irene Catuaí Catuaí is a cornerstone varietal of contemporary coffee production, prized for its resilience as much as its quality. While often associated with dependable everyday coffees, lots like this show just how expressive the variety can be when grown in exceptional conditions. A classic washed process brings clarity and structure to the cup, revealing vibrant citrus, rounded sweetness and a lingering, syrupy finish.

items.desc: Tanzania — Edelweiss Estate Geisha Although Geisha's route from Ethiopia to Central and South America passed through Tanzania, the varietal has remained largely absent from the country's coffee landscape. At Edelweiss, Neel and Kavita have reintroduced Geisha, sourcing and cultivating the seeds themselves to establish the variety on the estate. Fully ripe cherries undergo a four-day pre-fermentation beneath a black tarp, where consistent airflow supports a controlled fermentation. items.title: Guatemala — Finca Gascón
items.desc: Guatemala — Finca Gascón This Catuai lot is processed as a natural, meaning the cherries are dried whole, with the fruit left intact around the seed. After harvest, the cherries are sorted, weighed and transported to the wet mill, before undergoing a 96-hour fermentation in GrainPro bags. Felipe has refined this approach over the years, drawing from a broad set of processing protocols to produce coffees with structure and sweetness. For this coffee, the result is a cup with vivid red fruit, subtle boozy notes and a sweet, rounded finish.

items.desc: Colombia — Linarco Rodriguez Pink Bourbon Pink Bourbon has become one of Colombia’s most sought-after varieties, prized for its clarity, floral aromatics and bright, structured acidity. The lot underwent an open fermentation for around 48 hours at approximately 15°C. Once fermentation is complete, the coffee is washed and transferred to covered dryers where it dries slowly for 25 days at temperatures between 18–22°C. items.title: Colombia — Linarco Rodriguez Castillo
items.desc: Colombia — Linarco Rodriguez Castillo This lot comes from producers across Huila, which are brought to Linarco’s farm for processing. The cherries are fermented between 14–22 °C for around 72 hours, before being pulped and left to oxidise for 48 hours. The result is a beautifully structured washed profile. Sweetness and fruit clarity are complemented by a gentle creaminess and a lingering, balanced finish.

items.title: Mexico — Benancio Chavez
items.desc: Mexico — Benancio Chavez This lot is processed using a semi-washed (honey) method, where the coffee cherry is pulped but a layer of sticky mucilage is intentionally left on the parchment during drying. After harvest, the cherries are rested intact for 24 hours, allowing the natural sugars to develop before pulping. Retaining this mucilage further enhances this lot's inherent sweetness. Drying takes place in Benancio’s solar dryer, where controlled conditions result in a cup that’s deliciously sweet and silky smooth.

items.title: Mexico — SIPRO
items.desc: Mexico — SIPRO This lot is naturally processed, where the coffee is dried whole in the cherry after harvest. With the fruit left intact, sugars are absorbed back into the seed as it dries, building depth and intensity of flavour. The result is a cup full of fruit-forward sweetness, with notes of dried fruit and a dense, syrupy texture. This is the fourth year in a row we’ve shared this coffee with you and once again, it’s a real standout.

items.title: Tanzania — Edelweiss Estate Mielado
items.desc: Tanzania — Edelweiss Estate Mielado Bourbon N39 is a Tanzanian Bourbon, first developed in the 1930s for quality and yield. This lot underwent an extended, high-temperature fermentation. Cherries were held for six days in a controlled, exothermic environment, where elevated temperatures drove the development of complex, fruit-forward esters while reinforcing the variety’s natural sweetness and structure. Following fermentation, the cherries were pulped, leaving a measured amount of mucilage intact. The result is a velvety, smooth cup with stone fruit sweetness and a slight nuttiness.

items.desc: Fruit Cake is a little slice of holiday comfort. Juicy pineapple and golden raisin bring a rich, fruit-forward sweetness, while chocolate caramels melt into a smooth, indulgent finish. A festive cup that feels right at home alongside your favourite holiday treats.

Its full body and gentle acidity create a velvety, luxurious cup with lingering sweetness and depth. This lot is processed with a focus on preserving the natural richness and complexity of the Pacamara variety.
