items.title: Second Slice / Costa Rica
items.desc: Second Slice is pure comfort in a cup. Warm cinnamon and baked apple pie bring the sweetness, while toasted pecan adds a rich, nutty finish. A cozy Costa Rican coffee that tastes like going back for another piece.

items.title: Sundae Drive / Papua New Guinea
items.desc: Sundae Drive is a sweet little escape to the lush highlands of Papua New Guinea. Creamy vanilla and rich caramel melt into warm, toasty pecan, creating a comforting cup that feels like dessert without ever being too much.

items.title: Favourite Pear / Burundi
items.desc: Favourite Pear is soft, elegant, and quietly comforting. Juicy pear sweetness drifts through delicate notes of Earl Grey, while a smooth touch of vanilla rounds out the cup with warmth and grace. This Burundi coffee feels familiar from the very first sip—gentle, refined, and easy to fall in love with.

items.title: Full Bloom / Colombia
items.desc: Full Bloom bursts open with vibrant hibiscus florals and the bright sparkle of clementine, balanced by a soft almond sweetness that lingers gently on the finish. Delicate yet expressive, it’s a cup that captures the feeling of spring at its peak—colourful, lively, and full of possibility.

items.title: Jam Jar / Ethiopia
items.desc: Jam Jar is bursting with the kind of sweetness that keeps you coming back for more. Juicy blueberry jam meets rich chocolate and a drizzle of buttery toffee, creating a cozy, indulgent cup with all the charm of a homemade treat. A little sweetness worth savouring, straight from Ethiopia.

Its medium body and balanced acidity highlight the elegance and complexity of this high-grown Geisha. items.title: Cherry Wild / Colombia
items.desc: Cherry Wild is a celebration of Colombia’s vibrant coffee spirit—lively, sweet, and just a little untamed. Bursting with ripe cherry brightness, the cup carries the rich, spiced depth of fruitcake, lifted by a sparkling hint of tangerine.

items.title: Currant Mood / Kenya
items.desc: Currant Mood is vibrant and expressive, like the first warm day after a long winter. Juicy blackcurrant leads the way, lifted by bright grapefruit acidity and softened with a creamy touch of vanilla. It’s lively, layered, and impossible to forget.

items.title: Sweet Tooth / Guatemala
items.desc: Sweet Tooth is made for those moments when a little indulgence goes a long way. Smooth milk chocolate and buttery caramel bring the comfort, while ripe yellow plum adds a juicy sweetness that keeps every sip feeling fresh. A wonderfully balanced Guatemalan coffee that’s hard to resist.

items.title: Drizzle Honey
items.desc: Drizzle Honey is raw, unheated honey that supports Canadian beekeepers. Healthy enzymes, vitamins and minerals are plentiful and you’ll get more natural flavour from spring pollen and nectar. For our fan favourite cafe beverage, the Sweet Latte, we add Drizzle White Honey to espresso and mix with silky textured steamed milk.

items.title: Santa Lucia / Brazil
items.desc: This natural Yellow Bourbon offers a taste reminiscent of a decadent chocolate dessert from your favourite restaurant. Its richness in flavour, smooth texture, low acidity, and heavier mouthfeel deliver comforting notes of chocolate and almond.

items.title: Hideaway / Dark
items.desc: Hideaway is your go-to dark roast for those moments when only the richest, most comforting coffee will do.

items.title: Daydream / Light
items.desc: Let your thoughts drift with Daydream. Daydream is your invitation to pause and reflect, perfect for moments when you need a gentle lift.

items.title: Two Wheel / House
items.desc: Kick start your day with a dynamic ride. Two Wheel is like a morning ride through your favourite part of town, energizing and full of life.

items.title: Off Hours / Decaf Coffee
items.desc: Unwind anytime with a decaf that’s rich in flavour, without the caffeine. Off Hours is perfect for those late-night moments or anytime you need a break without the buzz; it’s decaf done right.

items.title: Homebody / Medium
items.desc: Homebody is like your favourite spot on the couch – always welcoming and perfectly cozy, ideal for thriving in your safe space.

items.title: KENYA Gondo AA
items.desc: Gondo AA comes from Gondo Factory in Murang’a County, on the western slopes of the Aberdare Mountains. The factory is one of three managed by the New Kiriti Farmers Cooperative Society, and it receives cherry from 727 smallholder farmers in the surrounding area. Most farms are small, often averaging around 250 coffee trees, and the cool temperatures, regular rainfall, and deep red volcanic soils help the coffee mature slowly. items.title: COLOMBIA La Violeta Sidra
items.desc: La Violeta is one of Rafael Aya Martínez’s farms in La Florida, near Timaná in southern Huila. This year, we stayed overnight on the farm, walked the land with Rafael, cupped through his coffees together, and visited his new café in Timaná. The visit gave us a clearer view of how his work connects cultivation, processing, and the local coffee culture he is helping build around his own coffees. Rafael began working in coffee as a picker at 15. By 21, he had saved enough to buy his first hectare of land, which he planted with Caturra. items.title: ETHIOPIA Esayas Beriso
items.desc: This coffee comes from Esayas Beriso in the Hambela Wamena district of Oromia, Ethiopia, at 2,350 masl. It is a natural process coffee from Ethiopian Landrace trees, and Esayas is the farmer behind Boku. The farm is listed under his own name, Esayas Beriso. He began in Dimtu, first working in a government office and then entering coffee through cherry collection with his brothers. He planted his own coffee trees and left his government position in 2009 to focus fully on coffee farming. items.title: GUATEMALA Buena Vista Pacamara Natural
items.desc: In the Fraijanes region of Guatemala, close to the city of Santa Rosa, the Buena Vista farm is located. The humid climate of the Fraijanes plateau with its sunny afternoons makes for the perfect combination for coffee plants to thrive and subsequently be fully sun-dried. Fredy Orantes, the owner of the farm, is a true leader among the coffee growers of Santa Rosa, and has worked tirelessly to maintain high standards in the field and during the harvest. items.title: COLOMBIA Manos Juntas – Holiday
items.desc: The Manos Juntas micromill can be found in the Sotara area of Colombia’s Cauca region. The region stretches from the western Cordillera Mountains to the Pacific Ocean and is characterized by the Popayan plateau, many rivers, and the central volcanic mountain range. Operated and managed by Banexport, the micromill’s entire concept is based on simplifying tasks and responsibilities, for both the producers and Banexport. items.title: ETHIOPIA Tadese Teko – Holiday
items.desc: From the highlands of Shale, a small village near Worka in Southern Ethiopia, this washed lot comes from Tadese Teko’s eight-hectare farm—a size notably larger than the regional average. His farm sits between 1,780 and 2,100 masl, rooted in deep red clay soils and surrounded by dense native vegetation. This coffee is part of a Single Farmer Project, a structure designed to provide traceability and market access for individual Ethiopian producers. items.title: COLOMBIA Chiroso Imperial
items.desc: Chiroso Imperial is the result of a partnership between four neighboring coffee growing families of Hub Management Palestina, including Ramón Gómez of Finca La Moreira. Grown on loamy clay to clay soils with volcanic ash and gravelly sectors, the coffee benefits from shade practices that protect the soil and support consistent development. Processing is precise: cherries are harvested based on color and Brix levels, floaters are removed through balseo, and uniformity is ensured with manual selection. Reaching the farm means a long drive along winding roads before the landscape opens to exposed slopes and narrow ridges planted with Pink Bourbon. items.title: COLOMBIA Finca Pensilvania Laurina
items.desc: Laurina, also known as Bourbon Pointu, is a rare natural mutation within Arabica, distinguished by its naturally low caffeine content and unique plant structure. This lot is a honey, where Moata used a hand disk pulper with no further soak, and laid the parchment out on raised beds, covered with shade mesh during the day, and opening the netting at dusk and overnight, resulting in things like nougaty white mulberry, taffy and oolong.

items.desc: A little Christmas ritual for someone you love. Or twelve very good reasons to keep the box for yourself. The 12 days of Christmas technically start on the 25th of December - so this is not an advent calendar - but designed to be enjoyed afterwards. Maybe shared with family and friends, maybe not! Inside are twelve different geisha coffees, each in a 30g pouch: enough for two 15g brews. All are roasted very light, looking for bright clarity and enough sweetness to support a clean profile. items.title: Janson Washed Geisha #232
items.desc: Kai and Jannette Janson are the main people behind Janson Family Estates - and are two of the loveliest people in Panama. They've been running the operations at the farm, located in the town of Volcan, for many years now - preceded by generations in the Janson family. This coffee is grown at their HACSA farm, around 1600m, which is right behind their processing factory, and offers amazing growing conditions for their Green Tip Geisha. items.title: Danche Hydro Honey
items.desc: We're welcoming in a new lot that we haven't worked with this producer before, and we've got to say - it's something very special! This is from the Danche Washing Station, in Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia, very closely located to the Chelbesa stations. The cherry here is sourced from 810 registered growers in the villages Danche and Kubi, in Gedeo zone, Gedeb. The average elevation of the farms lies at around 2100 Meters Above Sea level on rich and fertile red soil in a semi-forested environment, and harvest takes place between November and January. Cherry variety is Mixed Heirloom / Ethiopian Land Ra

items.title: Kiandu AA Washed
items.desc: Great, classic washed Kenyan coffees are getting harder and harder to find unfortunately. Subtle changes to farming practices, environmental reasons, and changes to varieties mean that the classic Kenyan profile of old is much more rare. This Kiandu AA lot is a great representation of how great and fruity Kenyan Washed coffees can be! Kiandu is a high-quality washing station in the Tetu area of Nyeri County, on the southern slopes of Mount Kenya. items.title: Bambito Estate Geisha Washed (Competition Lot)
items.desc: Ever since first trying Ivan and Priscilla's coffee's in 2022, we loved what they produced. Their elusive Washed Geisha is a rare lot that speaks for itself in quality and elegance - something super special, and worth appreciating! Grown in Bambito, nearby Volcan in Panama (just off the road leading to Cerro Punta), the land where their geisha grows goes up the mountain to around 1800m above sea level. items.title: Alo Main Station Dark Room Dry Natural
items.desc: From the main station of Alo Village, and a producer we've worked with for several years now, comes a very special lot that represents how much Tamiru Tadesse has pushed processing at Alo. This lot is a classic natural, without extra fermentation but has a special dark room drying. Tamiru built these dark rooms for drying coffee a few years ago, but has expanded them recently to accomodate more lots, and we were lucky enough to get this one, lot #34. items.desc: This is your answer to a daily coffee that's good on price, giving a dependable flavour profile, and enjoyable every day without being too much. Mama Sierra, led by Sirley Pulgarin of The Coffee Quest Colombia, is a remarkable project empowering women coffee farmers in the community of Giraldo, Antioquia. With 15 motivated members, the project began in March 2021, initiated by Yessica Parra and later taken forward by Sirley. items.title: Kotowa Las Brujas Geisha Clean Natural
items.desc: This year is the first year we're buying from Kotowa Farms in Boquete, and we're absolutely thrilled to offer this amazing Geisha from their Las Brujas farm lot 26-094! This lot in particular is their outstanding Geisha, which was processed with a "Natural" process, although the result in the cup is something that reminds us much more of a washed. We had confirmed with the farm that it was infact a natural, even though it does appear more washed. items.title: Chilaka Anaerobic Natural
items.desc: Tamiru Tadesse is a coffee supplier who has been in the coffee business for the last eight years. He works with about 200 farmers in Delo Kebele, Bensa zone of the Sidama region. He collects about 182,000 kilograms of red cherry from an estimated 80 hectares of land owned by the farmers. Tamiru processes anaerobic and natural coffee which is dried on a raised bed with mesh wire. He then sells his coffee on the international market, mostly in China. items.title: Altieri Pre-dry Natural Geisha DFM
items.desc: This is our first year visiting and buying from the Altieri farm in Boquete, and it was an absolute treat. Getting to see their facilities, and cup their outstanding lots from a variety of processes and elevations is really impressive! We purchased a few lots from them, and the first to be released is this pre-dry natural Geisha. This lot is from their Tom lot - it sits around 1700m above sea level at Alto Quiel, in Boquete, Panama. It covers an area of approximately 1 hectare of volcanic soil where Geisha Green Tip grows. It is adjacent to the protected area of the Volcan Baru national park,

items.title: Guji Rassa Washed
items.desc: This is a classic washed Ethiopian coffee that ticks all the boxes. You can imagine that when someone says "washed Ethiopian coffee" you have a profile in mind - this is exactly that - nothing more, nothing less. Grown from 2000-2200masl in the village of Rassa, in the Guji region of Ethiopia, this lot is comprised of mixed heirloom varieties without specific selection of varieties that comes with several smallholder farmers producing cherries at a time. items.title: Chiroso Washed Las Perlitas
items.desc: A washed Chiroso from Las Perlitas in Antioquia, Colombia, sourced through Coffee Quest. Smallholder deliveries are cupped separately and combined when their profiles complement one another. Bright, juicy and sweet, with orange, prune and almond in the cup. We roast it to work beautifully as both filter and espresso.

items.title: Cherry Ripe Blend
items.desc: This coffee is born out of a simple question - how can we make an espresso blend that's the most fruity as possible, while still being clear and clean. We have been working on this lot for several months, starting right from sourcing. We worked hand in hand with our friends at Cofinet to source these components and design this blend around 3 particular lots. Firstly a Washed and Natural Caturra - these set the base for our blend providing a fruity, yet well structured base. items.title: Rose Rejects
items.desc: Rose Rejects is coffee that didn’t make it into our main lineup. It’s a mix of beans rejected by our colour sorter — including quakers and beans that are visually over-roasted — alongside roasted batches that missed our internal targets by being too light, too dark, or otherwise outside spec. Nothing unsafe, nothing adulterated, just coffee that didn’t meet the standard we set for Rose. This is not a curated blend and it’s not meant to be expressive or particularly tasty. Expect a very basic cup. Sometimes flat, sometimes rough, sometimes fine — but never special. If you’re looking for clarity

items.title: The House Blend
items.desc: This is a special "House Blend" that we've designed specifically for use on Espresso machines / Bialetti. It's an easy drinking coffee that has a well developed roast profile to make it easy to extract, while still keeping recognisable flavours of the origins. We would call this a "Medium - Dark" roast. Not so much that the beans are all oily, but developed enough to have Low Acidity, Smooth Body, and mostly chocolatey flavour notes. All the coffees we use in this are Specialty coffee, but with very approachable taste profiles and qualities. We've sourced these lots either direct from farmers,

items.title: The Bedtime Blend
items.desc: This is a blend that we've designed especially to be as delicious as non-decaffeinated coffee - to be used for Espresso/Bialetti brewing and goes amazing as both a black coffee, and with milk. We believe that decaffeinated coffee doesn't have to come at the sacrifice of quality - so we created this Decaf blend that is as delicious as full strength coffee. Generally you will find more sweetness and acidity, as the balance with the bitter caffeine has been removed. items.title: Duvis Moreno - Honduras
items.desc: This is our second consecutive year purchasing coffee from Duvis Moreno and his farm, Finca Las Tres Peñas, located in the village of El Cedral, in the region of Santa Barbara. Originally a vegetable farmer, Duvis briefly worked as a factory laborer in a nearby city until a serious workplace accident forced him to return home to recover. After his recovery, he decided to transition into specialty coffee production and transformed his small plot of land into a specialty farm planted entirely with Pacas. This lot is clean and structured, with warming notes of browning sugars and baking spice com

items.title: Abel Salinas - Ecuador
items.desc: Abel Salinas is an accomplished producer — winner of Ecuador’s 2021 Cup of Excellence competition — whose Mejorado lots we always look forward to cupping. Abel's farm, Finca Arashi, is located in the town of Saraguro, in Ecuador's famous Loja province, home to many exceptional coffee producers. On his seven hectares, Abel grows mostly Typica Mejorado, a variety that genetic testing has revealed to be not Typica at all but rather a cross of Bourbon and Ethiopian Landrace. items.title: Jingle Beans Holiday Blend
items.desc: Behold! A coffee is born. 'Tis the freaking season and what have you! Oh, Jingle Beans, oh Jingle Beans, our annual ho-li-day blend. Each year we go out of our way to make this blend as seasonally outlandish as we can. This year, two coffees from Ethiopia — a washed and a naturally processed — triumphantly coalesce into the best interpretation of drinkable fruit cake in a cup. Jingle Beans, Jingle Beans, Jingle all the beans.

items.title: David Muñoz - Honduras
items.desc: For the second consecutive year, we kick off Honduran season with a coffee from David Muñoz, a producer who’s been a mainstay on the Tandem menu for a decade. David grows multiple varieties on his roughly 3 hectare farm, Nueva Esperanza, in Santa Barbara, but the majority is Pacas. This 100% Pacas lot is soft and sweetness-driven. We taste a familiar, balanced cup with flavors of caramel, milk chocolate, toasted nuts, and gentle plum-like acidity.

items.title: Kibingo - Kenya
items.desc: This washed field blend from Kibingo Estate is another stellar coffee sourced via Kamavindi Coffee Labs. Established in 1957 with just 100 trees — the maximum allotment for Kenyan growers under colonial law at the time — Kibingo has since grown into one of the country’s most highly regarded estate farms. The estate won Kenya’s Taste of Harvest competition in 2024, and owner Anthony Kimani has continued investing in farm-level and processing infrastructure, with plans to expand beyond its current 6,000 trees. items.title: Oneska - Kenya
items.desc: Oneska is the small estate farm of Onesmus Njagi, a retired schoolteacher, and his wife, Karen, on the slopes of Mount Kenya in Embu County. Last fall, we visited ahead of harvest and toured their four hectares, where they grow the traditional SL-28 and SL-34 varieties at good altitude and under ideal growing conditions. The name Oneska is a portmanteau of Onesmus and Karen, who established the farm in the early 1990s and have spent decades honing their agronomic and processing practices. items.title: Heri Agena - Ethiopia
items.desc: This microlot is the first of four coffees we’ll feature this year from Karamo Coffee, a quality-driven export company working in the high-altitude regions of Bensa and Bura in Sidama. items.title: Danche Yellow Honey- Ethiopia
items.desc: This honey-processed Ethiopian coffee comes to us from Danche station in Gedeb, one of two sites operated by SNAP Specialty Coffee in the kebele of Chelbesa. Founded in 2019, Danche now processes cherry from approximately 800 nearby smallholder farmers, most of whom grow small amounts of coffee on 2-3 hectare plots of land at significant elevation. Danche began with a focus on washed lots but has since expanded to include natural, honey, and experimental preparations. items.title: Alma Pineda - Cup of Excellence - Honduras
items.desc: This year, we purchased a split share of Alma Pineda’s washed Gesha lot, one of our top-scoring coffees from the 2026 Honduras Cup of Excellence (CoE). Alma’s coffees have placed at the Honduras CoE before, including third in 2019 and second in 2024, with this lot placing eighth in the Exotic Varieties category. Her farm, El Limo, sits at 1650 masl in Santa Barbara, where nearly all the Honduran coffee on our menu is grown. items.title: Faver Ninco - Colombia
items.desc: This is the first of three Pink Bourbon lots we’ll be featuring from the main harvest at Finca Costa Rica, Faver Ninco’s 10-hectare farm in Santa Maria. At just over 2,000 masl, Finca Costa Rica experiences cooler temperatures than much of the region, with more limited sunlight and less regular rainfall. These factors combine to produce more sporadic flowering and nearly year-round picking. Within that fluid cycle, Finca Costa Rica still has a defined main harvest season that runs from May to August, with this first lot coming from the early and peak portions of the harvest. items.title: Sun Lamp Decaf
items.desc: “I might as well be drinking tea*,” you say to no one in particular as you drink another cup of lousy decaffeinated coffee. Don’t feel defeated by bad decaf. Turn to Tandem’s brighter, sweeter Sun Lamp. With hints of marshmallow, graham cracker and green grape, let the surprising flavors of Sun Lamp reimagine what decaffeinated coffee can be and leave the anxiety behind. *No offense to tea. We love tea.

items.title: West End Blues
items.desc: Traditional in name only, West End Blues is a complex blend of flavors and textures. Fruity but not fruit-forward, grounded in chocolate and sparkling with zesty notes of baking spices and tea, WEB shines when combined with milk but stands on its own as a killer drip coffee.

items.title: Stoker
items.desc: Sometimes you want a delicious, no-nonsense cup of coffee, beloved by metalheads and hardcore grandmothers alike. That’s why Tandem shed its “Light Roaster” mantle to create our version of a “Kinda Dark” roasted coffee. Inspired by late-night diner runs, hot donuts, and arctic blasts, Stoker’s pleasantly sweet roastiness will carry you through the day.

items.title: Time & Temperature
items.desc: Effervescent, electric, and just plain cool, Time and Temperature is Tandem’s signature espresso blend. Perfect for dancing alone or with friends, it doubles as a delightful drip coffee. However you enjoy its crisp acidity and punchy sweetness, it’s our embodiment of “Spreading Joy” in every cup.

items.desc: Kagere Factory er en vaskestasjon som ligger i Othaya i Nyeri County, et av Kenyas mest berømte kaffedistrikter. items.title: Kaffebønner Brasil Fazenda IP
items.desc: I 1967 etablerte Isidro Pereira kaffegården Fazenda IP. Etter å ha fullført landbruks- og gårdsstudier ble også sønnen Luiz Paulo Pereira Sr. med på laget. Rundt byen Carmo de Minas, ligger flere av de beste kaffegårdene i Brasil. The spicy notes of gingerbread, the bright acidity of cranberry, and the delicate sweetness of vanilla create a warm, harmonious blend, perfect for enjoying the most special moments of Christmas. To give as a gift, share, or simply savor.

Here, the cool climate, wide temperature swings, and fertile soils allow the cherries to ripen slowly, developing extraordinary aromatic complexity. The Heirloom varieties, ancient indigenous Ethiopian cultivars, give this coffee an elegant, nuanced profile that expresses the full character of its terroir. The washed process enhances its clarity and brightness, highlighting the transparency of its aromatic notes and the pleasant liveliness

items.title: Ethiopia Aricha Wubanchi
items.desc: A single-origin coffee from Aricha Wubanchi, in the heart of the Yirgacheffe region, grown at an altitude of 2,200 meters. Made from Heirloom varieties and processed using the washed method, this coffee showcases the finesse of Ethiopia’s high altitudes. A bright, clean cup where lively acidity intertwines with delicate sweetness. Notes of peach, lime, and berries come through on the palate, with an elegant, fresh, and lingering aromatic profile.

items.desc: We’re talking about the same botanical variety, Catuai, and the same processing method. The only difference is the fermentation method: this time, it’s 100% anaerobic fermentation, meaning entirely without oxygen. This coffee offers a rounder, more complex acidity, with fruity notes reminiscent of pineapple. Its sweetness is intense and recalls dried fruit, like raisins, with a rich body and a lingering, sweet, syrupy aftertaste, enriched with hints of honey.

The Marsellesa variety is processed using the Washed method, which helps enhance its clarity and aromatic definition. In the cup, it has a sweet, fresh, and fruity profile: citrus notes of orange meet the sweetness of red apple and cane sugar, creating a pleasant, harmonious balance. A coffee with a lively, well-defined character, where freshness and sweetness come together in a clean, balanced, enjoyable cup.

items.title: Honduras Finca El Puente • Anacafe • washed
items.desc: From Honduras, in the Marcala region, comes a coffee grown at Finca El Puente, at an altitude of 1,550 meters. The Anacafe variety, processed using the Washed method, produces a clean, sweet cup where hints of honey meet the smoothness of maple syrup and the rich notes of caramel. A profile built around sweetness, with full, harmonious flavors unfolding in the cup and leading to a pleasantly lingering finish.

The natural process brings out its sweeter, fruitier character, creating a rich cup full of nuances. At the first sip, rich, creamy notes of apricot yogurt emerge, blending gently with hints of banana before giving way to a delicate violet finish. A vibrant, enveloping, unforgettable cup that turns every sip into a moment to savor.

items.desc: From the highlands of Alto Quiel, Panama , at 1,700 meters, comes the Pacamara from Finca Lérida . Processed using the natural method, it offers a rich, fruity profile in the cup, where the sweetness of honey meets the juicy notes of plum and the aromatic brightness of orange peel . A coffee with a bold character that tells the full story of its origin.

items.title: Panama Finca Lerida • natural

Processed using the natural method, it reveals an intense, nuanced aromatic profile: the floral fragrance of jasmine opens the tasting, making way for the tropical sweetness of mango and the juicy brightness of blueberry . A medley of aromas that makes this cup complex and surprising, and a highlight of Best of Panama 2026.

items.title: Panama Finca Lerida • washed
items.desc: Fresh and floral, this Geisha Washed from Finca Lerida expresses all the finesse of Panama’s high altitudes. Grown at 1,700 meters in Alto Quiel, Panama , it has an aromatic profile in which freshness and sweetness alternate naturally. The first sip brings lively notes of blood orange , followed by the fruity delicacy of white peach . Honey completes the profile with a soft, lingering sweetness, accompanying the finish and enhancing the cup’s complexity. An expressive, balanced Geisha that surprises with every sip.
